pros: Drag-and-drop canvas makes ad hoc visual exploration fast
Level of detail expressions and table calculations handle hard analytical questions
Certified data sources and row-level security support governed self-service
Built-in geocoding and spatial file support make maps easy
Tableau Public and community forums answer most problems quickly
cons: Three per-user tiers get expensive once dashboards reach everyone
Data modelling is weaker than a dedicated semantic layer or warehouse
Learning curve is steep beyond the first simple chart
Large extracts and busy dashboards can slow down noticeably
verdict_line: Pick Tableau if your analysts explore data visually and you need polished, governed dashboards at scale.

pros: Pro seats at $14 per user let dashboards reach the whole company
Power Query and DAX tabular models handle star schemas and time intelligence
Reports embed in Teams and SharePoint, and Excel connects live to models
Premium per user lifts models to 100 GB and 48 refreshes a day
Copilot drafts DAX measures and narrative summaries on well-modelled data
cons: Power BI Desktop runs only on Windows, so Mac users work in the browser
DAX filter context produces wrong totals that are hard to spot
Copilot needs Fabric capacity or Premium per user, not the cheap tiers
Fabric capacity licensing is hard to estimate for large deployments
verdict_line: Pick Power BI if you already run Microsoft 365 and want governed dashboards in front of everyone at the lowest seat cost.

pros: Hundreds of prebuilt connectors sync a new SaaS source within minutes
Upstream schema changes propagate to the warehouse without pipeline edits
Log-based change data capture keeps load on production databases low
Connector SDK runs custom sources inside the same managed framework
dbt Core integration and Quickstart models deliver clean tables after loading
cons: Monthly active row pricing gets painful on event-heavy or high-churn tables
Extract and load only, so modelling still happens in the warehouse
Connector behaviour cannot be customised and bug fixes wait on Fivetran
Long-tail connectors are less mature than the flagship ones
verdict_line: Pick Fivetran if you want dependable managed connectors into your warehouse and would rather model data than maintain ingestion code.

pros: Messy CSV to first answer and chart takes a minute or two
Generated Python is visible, so wrong numbers can be traced and fixed
Regressions, significance tests and correlations come back with plain explanations
Sandboxed execution handles files that would freeze a browser spreadsheet
Persistent threads let you resume an analysis and build on earlier results
cons: No governed semantic models, scheduled dashboards or row-level security
Ambiguous columns or vague questions yield confident but wrong answers
Free plan message limits run out quickly with real work
Uploading files makes it easy to overshare sensitive data
verdict_line: Pick Julius if you want to question spreadsheets and CSVs in plain language and see the code behind every answer.
